ASCII FAST PATH: all-ASCII strings are reversed byte-by-byte, so CRLF is SPLIT ('a

reverse(123)/reverse(1.5)/reverse(true) are BinderExceptions (no implicit cast to VARCHAR; sole overload reverse(VARCHAR)->VARCHAR) — the specializer must reject or explicitly cast, not assume stringification.
reverse is NOT an involution: leading combining marks and odd regional-indicator counts re-cluster on the second pass (reverse(reverse(x)) != x).
summary: DuckDB 1.5.5 reverse() has two code paths. (1) If every character is ASCII, it byte-reverses — which splits CRLF ('a\r\nb' -> 'b\n\ra'), the only place it deviates from UAX-29 since ASCII has no other multi-char clusters. (2) Otherwise it reverses UAX-29 EXTENDED grapheme clusters exactly, byte-preserving each cluster with zero normalization: combining marks stay attached, degenerate leading marks are their own cluster, RIs pair greedily from the left (odd counts leave a trailing singleton), ZWJ emoji/keycap/VS sequences hold together, ZWJ after non-emoji travels with the preceding char, Hangul LVT jamo stay one cluster and are not composed, CRLF is one cluster, marks after CR/LF/controls stand alone, and U+0600 Prepend binds to the following char (proving extended, not legacy, clusters). Rust rule: `if s.is_ascii() { reverse bytes } else { unicode_segmentation::graphemes(s, true).rev().collect() }` reproduces every pin. NULL -> NULL; non-VARCHAR arguments are binder errors (no implicit cast), and reverse(reverse(x)) != x for leading-mark and odd-RI inputs.
